findings.title: Two gaps in the PHI-shape check on kept codes: Coverage skips it, and the redirect's check misses shapes written with the codes' own separators
findings.failure: Two ways this goes wrong. (1) Coverage reads the codes back with keptCodes alone (apps/web/src/components/coverage/letter.tsx:101), while refusalLocation also runs textPhiFindings (download-refusal.ts:105). So a crafted link like /p/<practice>/coverage?refused=invalid&fields=codes&codes=123456789 (or codes=19500115) puts a nine-digit run or an 8-digit date into the field, marked refused. The redirect itself would have dropped both values (probe at 63aaa7f4: the redirect's Location has no codes, but the page shows them). ADR 0079:171 says such a link places 'never a date, nine digits or another shape the PHI guard knows', which is false for the page. (2) The guard's SSN, phone and date shapes need '-', '.' or '/', and none of those is in the codes alphabet. So the 303 copies these into the Coverage URL: '123 45 6789' (SSN with spaces), '919,555,0100' or '919\t555\t0100' or '919<NBSP>555<NBSP>0100' (phone), '01 15 1950' (date). The Location becomes e.g. /p/<id>/coverage?refused=invalid&fields=codes&codes=123+45+6789. That URL then stays in the address bar, because a marked field renders no ForgetRefusal. It is logged a second time and contradicts the PR body's 'Any value with an identifier's shape is dropped'. The GET form already sends the codes in the request URL, so this is defense in depth against the CLAUDE.md rule against PHI in a URL, not a new exposure class.
findings.fix: Put the check inside keptCodes, so the redirect and the page share one rule. After the alphabet and token-length tests, return undefined when textPhiFindings(codes).length > 0 || textPhiFindings(codes.replace(/[\s,;]+/g, '-')).length > 0. Reading the separators as '-' lets the SSN, phone and date shapes see '123-45-6789', '919-555-0100' and '01-15-1950'. Over 200,000 generated valid lists of 5-character codes this flags 0, and it still keeps 'ABC', '97110, 97530' and 'g0283;97110'. Keep the textPhiFindings call in refusalLocation as a second check for the other kept values. Extend the DLR-03 test at download-refusal.test.ts:389 so keptCodes returns undefined for '123456789', '19500115', '123 45 6789', '919,555,0100', '919\t555\t0100' and '01 15 1950'. Add a letter.test.tsx case: a crafted codes=123456789 leaves the field without a value. Reword ADR 0079:171 to match.
findings.rule: CLAUDE.md Never: PHI in a URL; ADR 0079 D3 'the writer and the reader never differ'; security-reviewer.md: PHI in URLs

findings.title: returnParams says a repeated query key is none; it is actually the last value
findings.failure: routeRequest builds the query with Object.fromEntries(new URL(request.url).searchParams) (handler.ts:176), which keeps the last value of a repeated key. So ?codes=ABC&codes=DEF reaches the route and returnTo as 'DEF', and the probe's Location carries codes=DEF. The route and the redirect see the same value, so nothing is unsafe today. But the comment says the opposite of the code, and the page reader single() (letter.tsx:53) really does treat a repeated key as none. Someone who trusts the comment could later make returnTo rely on a property it does not have.
findings.fix: Change the comment to: 'The request's parameters as a returnTo reads them: the strings only, as the route reads them (a repeated query key is its last value; a catch-all array is dropped).'
findings.rule: maintainability: comments state what the code does

checkedSound: Applied the whole security-reviewer.md checklist. No migration, no new table, query, job, upload or model call. All checks still run in invoke and Postgres: a practice outside scope gives NotFoundError, the permission is checked before any lookup, and the page routes and their reads are unchanged. Nothing new is logged.

Open redirect: the Location path is built only by pagePath from route constants and opaqueId-validated, lowercased path parameters. Every template's [name] is a path parameter of its download route (checked against all 15 route files). Path parameters override query ones in routeRequest. safeReturnPath re-checks the path. Probed with the real code: //evil.example, /\evil, %2F%2F (as a decoded path param), dot segments (/p/.., /p/%2e%2e), unicode slashes (U+2215, U+FF0F), uppercase IDs, an array (catch-all) param, __proto__ and constructor keys, 5,000-character codes and CRLF in codes. Each gives '/', is dropped, or is encoded by URLSearchParams. Kept keys are route constants, so a refusal-key collision is impossible and filtered anyway.

No existence oracle: another practice's ID, another practice's object (hidden by row-level security) and a malformed ID all give not_found, as nonexistent ones do. A viewer is refused by permission before any lookup. The landing page applies its own check (404 or Forbidden) before any notice renders. Cross-site, COOP same-origin severs a popup on both the JSON and the 303 path, and an iframe (Dest iframe) gets JSON while XFO DENY and frame-ancestors 'none' block framing, so the refusal type can't be told apart from another site.

Content spoofing: notices come only from the closed status list (downloadRefusalParams, with .catch on every key). The only text from the URL that reaches the screen is the codes input's value, in the letters, digits and separators alphabet, which ADR 0079 accepts as a residual (SEC-01 tightens it). Payer and contract are selected only from the form's own options.

Referrer: next.config sends Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin on every response, including the 303. The page CSP allows only self and Stripe, so neither the refused URL nor the landing URL leaks a path or query to a third party. ForgetRefusal's replaceState writes only the current same-origin pathname, search and hash.

CSRF and state: the change records nothing new. A refusal happens before or instead of the export record; a success is the same attachment. HEAD and POST are still refused with 405 before the route runs (test passes). No download is linked through next/link, so nothing is prefetched. Downloads need no CSRF token, so csrf_refused and duplicate can't occur on them. Pre-existing and unchanged: download GETs don't check Sec-Fetch-Site, so a cross-site top-level navigation with SameSite=Lax cookies can trigger a download, and with it an export record.

The 303 carries the request's Set-Cookie lines (a session refresh or deletion) and cache-control private, no-store, with no body and no content-type. Its relative Location passes through the standalone Next server unchanged (the e2e asserts the exact relative header). proxy.ts never touches a route handler's response except to add the CSP.

isNavigation: a page script cannot set Sec-Fetch-* (forbidden header names), and browsers that support it always send Sec-Fetch-Mode on fetch(). A script that pretends to navigate, using Accept in an old browser or curl with forged headers, gets a 303 to a page it could open anyway, with less detail than the JSON (no message, roles or suspension reason). Uppercase or empty mode values read as a script.

Pages that now read searchParams don't change what they read or audit. loadPage passes the query to non-strict z.object schemas, which strip refused, fields and retry. No return page's params schema has a key named payer, contract, codes, list or from. month (monthly) and version (packet) are the pages' own validated parameters.
signInFor moved to sign-in-for.ts with its logic unchanged; its reason values are a closed set. Regexes (REFUSED_FIELD, CODES, QVALUE, safeReturnPath) are linear with no catastrophic backtracking.

review-security.summary:
Security review of PR #78 at 63aaa7f4 found no blocking issue: one should-fix and two nits. The 303 can't be made into an open redirect. Its path is built only from route constants and validated IDs, and the handler checks it again; every hostile input I tried (encoded and double slashes, dot segments, unicode lookalike slashes, CRLF, very long values, prototype keys, uppercase or array IDs, a query key that collides with a path parameter) lands on '/' or is dropped. A refusal reveals no more than today's JSON did. Tenancy and permission checks are unchanged in the handler and Postgres, pages read and audit the same things, nothing new is recorded or logged, and the security-relevant tests pass (7 files, 235 tests).

**Should-fix (SEC-01): the check that drops identifier-shaped codes has two gaps.**
- Coverage reads kept codes back without the check the redirect applies. A crafted link can therefore put a nine-digit run or an 8-digit date into the field, which ADR 0079 line 171 says can't happen.
- The redirect's own check misses SSN, phone and date shapes written with spaces, commas, tabs or non-breaking spaces. '123 45 6789' and '919,555,0100' are copied into the Coverage URL.
- Fix: one rule inside keptCodes that also checks the value with its separators read as '-'. It flagged 0 of 200,000 generated valid code lists. Correct the ADR line and add tests.

**Nits:**
- SEC-02: when a refusal on Coverage shows a notice instead of marking a field, the kept codes and IDs stay in the URL, where they no longer do anything.
- SEC-03: a comment in handler.ts (line 302) says a repeated query key is dropped; the code keeps its last value.

Separate from this PR and unchanged by it: download links don't check where the request came from, so a link on another site can make a signed-in person's browser download a file and record the export. That fits a follow-up rather than this PR.

(1) apps/web/src/lib/http/handler.ts:176 builds `query = Object.fromEntries(new URL(request.url).searchParams)`. I ran this under node with `?codes=ABC&codes=DEF&k=1` and got `{ codes: 'DEF', k: '1' }`, so the last value of a repeated key wins.

(2) handler.ts:177 merges `{ ...query, ...context.params }`. Path parameters win over a query key with the same name, which is sound. handler.ts:357 passes this same `built.params` to `refusedNavigation`. invoke.ts:99 parses the same object with the route's params schema. So the route and returnTo see the same value.

(3) The comment at handler.ts:302 says "(a repeated query key is none)". The filter at handler.ts:305 drops only values that are not strings, which in practice means a catch-all's string[]. A repeated query key reaches returnTo as its last value. `git diff e908c214` shows this PR added the comment, so it is new and it is false.

(4) A concrete case: coverage.ts:198-205 (payerLetter). With `?payer=<id>&codes=ABC&codes=DEF` and a refusal, the route parses codes='DEF', `keptCodes('DEF')` keeps it, and the 303 Location carries `codes=DEF` once. The page then reads one value. The route and the page agree, and `keptCodes` holds the value to its closed alphabet. Nothing is unsafe or misleading on screen, and a repeated key only comes from a hand-made URL, since the GET form has one codes input.

(5) The confusion is real. letter.tsx:52-56 `single()` and its comment "a repeated key is none" do describe the page side correctly, because Next gives a string[] there. ADR 0079 section 5 and download-refusal.ts:123 say the same, but only about the page's reader. The design doc and the PR body say nothing about returnParams, so the code is not required to drop repeated keys. The comment is wrong; the code is not.

The fix is the right kind, and making the code drop repeated keys would be worse. routeRequest is shared by every GET and PUT route. The route has already parsed the last value, so a returnTo that dropped it could send the person back without the value the route actually refused. That loses information and creates a split between the route and the page.

The reviewer's wording is accurate. I would make it slightly more precise: say it is the same object the route's schema parsed, and that a path parameter wins.

Sound otherwise:
- path parameters cannot be overridden from the query;
- non-string values are dropped before returnTo;
- a returnTo that throws gives null (handler.ts:313-317);

I could not refute it. Everything below was checked at 63aaa7f4 in a fresh clone (scratchpad/verify-ux02). Progress is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/12cbf3a7-985c-52b3-adc0-b6d7ac05d769/scratchpad/progress/dlr-verify-ux-UX-DLR-02.md.

What the code does:
- The diff removes `download` from receipts.tsx:181 (Report, now reportHref(...)) and from packet/[versionId]/review/page.tsx:129 and :138 (PDF and CSV). This is ADR 0079 D4.
- handler.ts:293-300 isNavigation: a request with Sec-Fetch-Mode navigate and Dest document (or no Dest) gets the 303 back to the page with ?refused=. A link with `download` sends Dest empty, so it gets JSON instead.
- No beforeunload handler exists anywhere in apps/web/src.
- uploader.tsx:111-139 sends each file as an XHR PUT, three at a time. Batches go up to 100 files and 2.0 GiB, so a batch can be in flight for minutes.
- The receipts list is drawn inside the Uploader, right under the drop zone (uploader.tsx:455; shot p.uploads.default.1280).

The refusal you can actually reach is rate_limited. The 'export' bucket in rate-limit.ts:44 allows 60 per user and 300 per address per 10 minutes, and 16 download routes share it, including the receipt report (uploads.ts:378). One office behind a single address could plausibly hit 300. not_found and forbidden are rarer.

Browser probe (Chromium 141, standalone server, synthetic data; scratchpad/verify-ux02-probe/probe.log):
- A: a link without `download` whose response is an attachment stays on the same document, and the in-flight PUT completes. So successful downloads are fine.
- B: the same link answered with a 303 to HTML loads a new document, and the server logged the PUT as aborted. This is the failure the finding describes.
- C: a beforeunload guard fires its dialog even on a successful no-`download` click. So the guard is only safe once Report stops navigating, as the finding says.
- D/E: with `download` the page never navigates (the shape before this PR).

Export review:
- The 7 required confirm_<id> boxes (review/page.tsx:359) only appear once both files have been downloaded (:333). After that, a refused re-download reloads the page and clears every tick.
- This trigger is narrower (a re-download after the boxes appear, plus the rate limit), but it is real.

Severity: should-fix is right. It is a regression introduced by this PR that throws away files the person chose. The trigger is narrow and the files can be picked again, so it falls short of blocking. Before the PR the refusal saved a JSON file: poor, but it lost nothing. Neither ADR 0079 nor the design discusses losing live state.

Sound:
- The 303 path for plain pages.
- Success downloads without `download` stay on the page.
- The refusal words exist (downloadRefusalWords, download-refusal.tsx:28).
- The JSON refusal body carries the outcome and Retry-After (handler.ts:78-86).

The fix is right in kind: intercept the click and fetch, keep the href, and add the beforeunload guard only after the intercept is in. I compared two other options and rejected both. Putting `download` back brings back the JSON-file refusal. target=_blank opens a second Uploads page in a new tab.

The fix needs these changes:
(1) Name the saved file from the response's Content-Disposition (handler.ts:365 sets attachment; filename=...). Otherwise the blob saves under a UUID name.
(2) Revoke the object URL after a tick (setTimeout), not synchronously.
(3) For outcomes the notice cannot settle (signed_out, maintenance), call location.assign(href). The server's own flow then handles sign-in.
(4) On the export review, after a successful fetch, call router.refresh() when downloadedBoth was false, so the checklist appears without the 'Then reload this page' step. The uncontrolled ticks survive the refresh.
(5) lib/http/download-refusal.ts imports @tp/observability, ./rate-limit and ./sign-in-for, so it is not client-safe. Move RefusedDownload, minutesWords and retryMinutes into a client-safe module, and import from it in both download-refusal.tsx and the new client component.
(6) Cover the reports reviewer checklist with the same wrapper. reports/[reportId]/review/page.tsx:48 and :52 never had `download`, and its required confirm_<id> boxes (:115) lose their ticks the same way. That is not a regression; before the PR a refusal there opened a JSON page.
(7) Add tests, and amend ADR 0079 D4. No current e2e covers Uploads or either review; DLR-04 covers only the Coverage letter and the report CSV.
verify-ux-UX-DLR-02.fix:
Add a client component, components/download-link.tsx ('use client'), with props href, children and an optional onDownloaded. It renders <a href={href}>, so a new tab, a modifier-click or a page without script still gets the 303 path.

On a plain primary click (button 0, no meta, ctrl, shift or alt key):
1. Call preventDefault, then fetch(href, { credentials: 'same-origin', headers: { accept: 'application/json' } }). Sec-Fetch-Mode is cors and Dest is empty, so isNavigation is false and the response is the JSON outcome.
2. If the response is ok:
   a. Read the filename from Content-Disposition, falling back to the last path segment.
   b. Build a blob and an object URL. Click a temporary <a download={filename}> with that URL, then revoke the URL in a setTimeout.
   c. Call onDownloaded.
3. If it is a refusal:
   a. Parse { outcome } and Retry-After.
   b. For signed_out or maintenance, call location.assign(href).
   c. Otherwise render the words from downloadRefusalWords(...) with retryMinutes(retryAfterSeconds) in a role="alert" notice placed above the receipts or files. Focus the notice with tabIndex={-1}.

Move RefusedDownload, minutesWords and retryMinutes into a client-safe module (for example lib/http/download-refusal-words.ts). Import it from download-refusal.tsx and from the new component. Do not import lib/http/download-refusal.ts, which pulls in @tp/observability, rate-limit and sign-in-for.

Use DownloadLink in four places:
- receipts.tsx:181 (Report).
- packet/[versionId]/review/page.tsx:129 and :138, with onDownloaded calling router.refresh() when the viewer had not downloaded both files.
- reports/[reportId]/review/page.tsx:48 and :52. This one is not a regression, but its confirm_ ticks are lost the same way.

Then add a beforeunload guard in Uploader (uploader.tsx) that is active only while any PUT or complete is in flight. It is safe once Report no longer navigates on a plain click.

Add tests:
- A unit test for the click interception and the filename parse.
- An e2e on Uploads that starts a synthetic upload, forces a rate_limited Report and asserts the PUT completes, the files stay and the notice is focused.
- An e2e on the packet review that ticks the boxes, forces a refused re-download and asserts the ticks are kept.

Amend ADR 0079 D4: pages that hold live state download by fetch, and the href stays as the no-script and new-tab path. No migration.

verify-ux-UX-DLR-04.reasoning:
I could not refute the mechanism, and should-fix is the right severity. The example in the finding cannot happen as written, and its fix has two gaps. All line references are at 63aaa7f4, in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/12cbf3a7-985c-52b3-adc0-b6d7ac05d769/scratchpad/verify-uxdlr04.

Confirmed:
- apps/web/src/components/coverage/letter.tsx:97-104 and :59-76 are a server component. aria-invalid, the "Error:" paragraph, the error id in aria-describedby, autoFocus and the kept entries are all computed from searchParams. No client code ever changes them.
- apps/web/src/lib/http/handler.ts:365 sends a successful letter as `content-disposition: attachment`, so the browser stays on the page and the URL does not change. The PR's own e2e shows this: apps/web/e2e/download-refusals.spec.ts:172-177 expects the same URL after the download.
- ForgetRefusal (which takes the refusal keys out of the URL) renders only inside the notice (apps/web/src/components/download-refusal.tsx:80). letter.tsx:107 renders the notice only when nothing is marked. So a marked letter keeps refused= and fields= in the URL, and ADR 0079 lines 122-125 say this is deliberate. A reload therefore brings back the refused entry, still marked, over what the person corrected.

Where the finding is wrong:
- The 'ABC' example cannot come from the form. LETTER_CODES_PATTERN (apps/web/src/lib/contracts/letter.ts:39) accepts exactly what the route accepts, and the browser blocks the submit. The e2e has to set noValidate to get past it (spec:91-94). A codes mark comes only from a typed or crafted URL.
- The same state is reachable in a realistic way through the contract select. letter.tsx:125-138 lists every payer's contracts whichever payer is chosen. Payer A with a contract of payer B is refused by letterParties (apps/web/src/lib/routes/coverage.ts:175-176) with field 'contract'. The e2e drives exactly this case (spec:120-129), and the screen p.coverage.error-letter-contract.390 shows it. After the person corrects it and downloads, the select still reads "Error: The payer's contract: choose one of this payer's contracts, or None named." with aria-invalid=true, on a pair the route just accepted. A reload restores the wrong contract, marked.
- No test covers a successful download after a refusal. The download step (spec:170-177) starts from a clean URL.

Why the accepted residual does not hold:
- Design R16 and ADR 0079's Consequences and Revisit-when (lines 162-167 and 194) accept this because "ux-forms' Field clears a field's mark as the person types". At origin/co-001/ux-forms 4f0b526d that is not true. Field and SelectField get their marks from useFieldIssue (form-issues.tsx:74-79), which reads FormIssuesContext, the server action's state. There is no input or change handler that clears a mark, and ADR 0077 does not mention one. The letter is a GET download form with no action state, so moving it onto Field would clear nothing.

Severity:
- should-fix is right. The screen, and aria-invalid for a screen reader, show an error on a value the route accepted, and a reload restores the refused entry. That is a real misreport. No money, record or file is wrong, though: the person gets the correct letter, and the restored entry would only be refused again. So it is not blocking.

Gaps in the proposed fix:
- Part (1) clears a mark only when that same control is edited. A contract refusal is a refusal of the pair, and the message invites fixing it by changing the payer. If the person does that, the contract keeps its mark through the successful download.
- Part (2) writes payer, contract and codes back into the URL and says a reload "then shows what was last sent". At letter.tsx:100-101 a visit without a refusal keeps no entries, so the reload would show the default form. Making it true means reading the entries on every visit. That widens the crafted-link residual that ADR 0079 deliberately limits (lines 168-171: ?codes= is read back only beside a refusal): a link from another site could fill the form unmarked, as if the person had typed it.

Sound: the marks and messages are correct while the refusal is current; describedby puts the error first, then the hint; only the first marked control takes the focus; kept payer and contract values are used only when they are the form's own options; no URL text is said in words.

I tried to refute UX-DLR-01 and couldn't. The bug is real and I reproduced it. The suggested fix stops the replay, but on its own it causes a new problem.

What the code does at 63aaa7f4:
- forget-refusal.tsx:24 calls `replaceState(window.history.state, ...)`.
- Next's HistoryUpdater runs in a useInsertionEffect (app-router.js:74-111), so by the time ForgetRefusal's effect runs, the history state already carries `__NA`.
- Next's patched replaceState returns early for any `__NA` state (app-router.js:305). That early return skips `restore` (:277-281), so the router's canonicalUrl keeps `?refused=`.
- The patch is only installed in AppRouter's useEffect, which runs after the child effects on the hydration commit.
- refresh-reducer.js:58-59 refetches `state.canonicalUrl`, and HistoryUpdater writes it back to the address bar.
- server-action-reducer.js:75 also posts to `state.canonicalUrl`, so any server action on a page with a notice is a third trigger.

The triggers the finding names are real:
- export-status.tsx:22-32 refreshes every 5 s (export-attempts.ts:55) while an export is live. The packet page renders the notice (packet/page.tsx:572).
- uploader.tsx:257-262 refreshes when a batch settles.

What I reproduced (next 16.4.3, synthetic data, my own clone, logs in scratchpad/progress/uxdlr01-probe-*.log):
- Run A, reports page: arriving gives a clean URL and a focused notice. After `next.router.refresh()` the URL is `/reports?refused=not_found` again, and a reload shows the notice again.
- Run A, uploads page, using the real upload flow: arrive at `?refused=rate_limited&retry=3` and upload CAS-08 remit.835. When the batch shows 'Loaded 1 remittance', the URL has `?refused=rate_limited&retry=3` again, and a reload shows the out-of-date 'Wait 3 minutes'.
- This breaks the PR's own promise (forget-refusal.tsx:9-12, ADR 0079:122-125, PR body line 23). The e2e (download-refusals.spec.ts:202-211) only reloads straight after arrival, so it misses this.

Severity: should-fix is right. The notice that comes back is the one already shown, or one sent to a colleague in a copied link. No amount, stage or action is wrong, and the base branch showed a JSON page anyway. So this is a gap in the new feature, not a regression and not a blocker.

Is the fix the best one? No.
- Run B, the suggested change alone: the URL stays clean, but the notice disappears on the first router refresh (notices 0, focus moves to BODY). On the packet page with a live export that happens within 5 s; on Uploads it happens when the batch settles. That breaks ADR 0079:124 and :163 and forget-refusal.tsx:11 ('stays on screen, focused, until the person moves on'). The suggested e2e step would still pass with this regression.
- Run C/C2, the suggested change plus a client component that holds on to the notice it arrived with (useState): it now survives a refresh. But it also stays after a soft navigation to the same route with other search params, because the 16.4.3 router keys a page as `__PAGE__`, ignoring search params (create-router-cache-key.js). So packet/page.tsx:593's version links would keep a notice about a different version on screen.

  - Same-route soft navigation: the notice goes away.
  - Uploads: the URL stays clean when the batch settles, the notice stays, and the batch is kept.
  - A reload shows no notice. Back behaves as it does in the PR.

The setTimeout in the suggested change is required, from reading the code (not tested). Without it, `replaceState(null)` during hydration hits the browser's unpatched replaceState and wipes `__NA` and the tree from history state. A later Back into that entry would then hit `handlePopState(null)`, which returns early (app-router.js:62-65).
